verses.40:2: Bem-aventurado o que {intellegit} e o pobre: * no dia mau o livrará o Senhor.
verses.40:3: O Senhor o conserve, e {vivificet}, e o faça bem-aventurado na terra: * e não o entregue {inanimam} dos seus inimigos.
verses.40:4: O Senhor lhe leve {opem} sobre o leito da sua dor: * {versasti} toda a sua cama na sua enfermidade.
verses.40:5: Eu disse: Senhor, tende piedade de mim: * curai a minha alma, porque pequei contra vós.
verses.40:6: Os meus inimigos disseram males {mihi6}: * Quando morrerá, e perecerá o seu nome?
verses.40:7: E, se entrava para {videret}, falava coisas vãs: * o seu coração juntou iniquidade para si.
verses.40:8: Contra mim {susurrabant} todos os meus inimigos: * contra mim pensavam em {mihi8}.
verses.40:9: Estabeleceram contra mim uma palavra iníqua: * Acaso o que dorme não tornará a {resurgat}?
verses.40:10: {etenim} o homem da minha paz, em quem esperei: * que comia {panes}, engrandeceu contra mim {supplantatio}.
verses.40:11: Vós, porém, Senhor, tende piedade de mim, e {resuscita}: * e eu lhes retribuirei.
verses.40:12: Nisto conheci que {voluisti}: * porque o meu inimigo não se alegrará à minha custa.
verses.40:13: Mas a mim, por causa {innocentia}, amparastes: * e me firmastes {conspectu} para sempre.
verses.40:14: Bendito o Senhor, Deus de Israel, {asaeculo}: * {fiat}.

decisions.latin: qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem
decisions.why: intellégere → entender (glossary, working); *super* (ἐπί) makes it 'understand concerning', i.e. give thought to the poor man's case (DRB 'understandeth concerning'). *entender sobre* is not Portuguese; *entender alguém* is, and means to grasp his situation. MS1932 *cuida do* says the act of care, which the Latin does not name. The verse is an Alleluia verse and a Gradual (Pent01-0a, missa Sancti/04-28, 07-18 — grep), so it will be heard alone.

options.label: o que entende
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb; *super* absorbed into the direct object (grammar, D2).

options.label: o que atenta para
options.note: keeps the direction of *super*; loses the verb of understanding.

options.label: o que cuida do
options.note: MS1932; says what the Latin does not (care).

decisions.why: vivificáre → vivificar is the glossary's working word (row open; Ps 118 has it twelve times). A blind reader of Ps 118 listed it as unknown. 40:3 is the versicle said for the Pope in the Preces (Preces.txt — grep), so the three verbs *conserve … vivifique … faça bem-aventurado* will be said alone.

options.label: o vivifique
options.note: Ruling: one word for one, as in Ps 118.

options.label: lhe dê vida
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'give him life'; the row's option.

decisions.why: The Latin has *ánimam* (the Hebrew נפש) where the Greek has εἰς χεῖρας, 'into the hands'; the Latin is followed (rule 1). 26:12 *Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me* → *às almas dos que me atribulam* is the precedent. *ánima* here is the enemies' desire (DRB 'the will'; MS1932 *ao poder*, which is the Greek).

options.label: à vontade
options.note: DRB 'will' — the sense, not the word.

options.label: ao poder
options.note: MS1932 — the Greek's hands, not the Latin.

decisions.why: *ops* (help) + *ferre* (bring). *auxílio* is adjutórium's (glossary), so the noun takes the free *socorro*, and *ferre* keeps a verb of bringing. *O Senhor o socorra* would merge the noun into the verb.

options.label: lhe leve auxílio
options.note: MS1932 *lhe dê auxílio*; collides with adjutórium.

decisions.latin: univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus
decisions.why: The person switches to God (*versásti*), as in the Greek (ἔστρεψας); kept, with no pronoun supplied. *versáre* is to turn over and over: God has turned the sick man's bed, nursed him (MS1932's note: 'cercaste-o de todos os carinhos' — a gloss, not taken). stratum → cama (glossary row *lectus / stratum*, which names this verse). The Latin puts the bed first (*univérsum stratum ejus versásti*); the verb first is natural order (D2).

options.label: virastes
options.note: plainer; DRB 'turned'; heard as flipping it once.

decisions.why: A dative of disadvantage (κακά μοι). What they say is then quoted, and it is said *about* me in the third person (*Quando moriétur*), so *de mim* is the Portuguese; DRB 'against me'.

options.label: de mim
options.note: Ruling: *dizer males de* = speak ill of.

options.label: contra mim
options.note: DRB, MS1932 *falaram contra mim*; then 40:8's *contra mim* ×2 would make it three.

decisions.why: *vidéret* has no object; the visit to the sick man is meant (DRB 'to see me', MS1932 *a vêr-me*). Left without an object as the Latin leaves it.

The Latin's pleonasm (*egrédi foras*, ἐξεπορεύετο ἔξω) is kept: rule 2 keeps the Latin's repetitions, and the contrast inside / outside (*ingrediebátur … egrediebátur foras*) is the verse's point — at the bedside vain talk, outside the plotting. *Saía para fora* is a pleonasm school grammar marks; the subject is named so that the line is heard as the visitor's (the Latin's person continues from 40:7).

in idípsum is deferred (D9; glossary row open, proposal: persons together → *juntos*, one agent or a thing → *a um só tempo*). Here one man speaks *in idípsum*; the Greek ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό begins the next verse (Rahlfs: 'together … they whispered'), but the Latin joins it to his speaking. DRB 'spoke to the same purpose': the same end as his heart's gathered iniquity and the enemies' whispering that follows. *juntos* needs a plural; *a um só tempo* would say nothing here.

options.label: no mesmo sentido
options.note: Ruling: DRB 'to the same purpose'; *in* + accusative, *idípsum* 'the very same'. Chosen over *para o mesmo fim* for the rhyme *fim / mim* at two neighbouring finals.

options.label: para o mesmo fim
options.note: DRB's reading, but its final *fim* rhymes with 40:8's *mim* (checks).

options.label: de comum acordo
options.note: reads the Greek's 'together' into his speech; explains.

decisions.why: L&S: to whisper, mutter. The cognate keeps the sound; *murmurar* is murmuráre's (and *murmurar* is to grumble in Brazil); MS1932 *cochichavam* is colloquial.

The anaphora *advérsum me … advérsum me* is kept. *mihi* repeats the person a third time (κακά μοι); cogitáre → *pensar em* (row; 34:4b *cogitántes mihi mala → os que pensam em males contra mim*). With *contra mim* already said, *para mim* carries the dative. DRB drops it.

options.label: (dropped)
options.note: DRB 'they devised evils to me' keeps it; MS1932 drops *advérsum me* instead.

decisions.latin: Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
decisions.why: resúrgere → ressurgir (row open, which names 40:9). *adícere ut* is προστίθημι, 'do again': *tornar a*, as 9:39 *ut non appónat ultra* → *não torne mais a*. The question is left as open as the Latin's *numquid … non* (numquid → *acaso*, row): the enemies' taunt, or the answer the Church hears in it. *ressuscitar* is kept for resuscitáre (40:11).
étenim → *pois* (row). Here *et* is 'even' (καὶ γάρ; DRB 'For even'): the betrayal is the climax of the list. *até* carries it.

The plural is the Latin's (ἄρτους); in Portuguese *comer o pão de alguém* is the idiom for sharing his table, and *os meus pães* is heard as loaves. Number is grammar (D2; as D29 *sangue*). Jn 13:18 quotes the verse in other words (Clementine, fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-43-13.json: *Qui manducat mecum panem, levabit contra me calcaneum suum* — singular).

*supplantátio* is tripping by the sole or heel (*sub planta*); the Greek πτερνισμός is from πτέρνα 'heel', and Jn 13:18 says *calcaneum*. L&S gives only 'hypocritical deceit' for this verse — the sense, which MS1932 takes (*traição*). *Rasteira* is the heel-trip itself and, in Brazil, already the figure for a betrayal (*dar uma rasteira em alguém*), so the image and the sense stand in one word (rule 2: images stay). magnificáre → engrandecer (row); super me → *contra mim* (as *magna loqui super me*, D39). *sua* is supplied: Portuguese needs a determiner, the Latin has none.

options.label: a sua traição
options.note: MS1932; L&S's sense, without the image.

decisions.why: The cognate, as the resúrgere row foresaw (*ressuscitar* kept for resuscitáre). In the psalm it is 'raise me from this bed' (MS1932's note); the Church sings it on Holy Saturday (Quad6-6: *R. Et resúscita me, et retríbuam eis* — grep), and the Latin word carries both. Safe at the *vós* imperative with the enclitic (D13).

options.label: levantai-me
options.note: DRB 'raise me up again' — closes the Latin's double sense on the sickbed.

decisions.why: velle → querer (row); 17:20 *quóniam vóluit me → porque me quis* is the precedent, heard there as 'loved me / chose me'. τεθέληκάς με. DRB 'hast had a good will for me'.

options.label: me quisestes bem
options.note: DRB's sense; the row's option at 21:9 (*lhe quer bem*).

decisions.why: The Latin has no possessive (the Greek: διὰ τὴν ἀκακίαν); DRB and MS1932 supply 'my'. Left as the Latin has it: whose innocence is plain from *a mim*, and the Church uses the verse of saints (missa Sancti/06-21, the Offertory; Hildegard's office — grep).

decisions.latin: et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum
decisions.why: confirmáre with a person as object → *firmar* (the row's proposal after 36:17 and 37:3: *confirmar* is heard as attesting). in conspéctu: the row's split — *à vista de* as a predicate, *na … presença* beside a verb of setting or worship (17:7b, 21:28b, 118:168–170); here God sets a man before him (Hebrew 'before your face'). in ætérnum → *para sempre* (D23).

options.label: diante de vós
options.note: MS1932 *diante de ti*; the row keeps *diante de* for *ante*.

decisions.latin: a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum
decisions.why: The first of three places (40:14, 89:2, 105:48); D37 rules *usque in sǽculum → para todo o sempre* and leaves the first member to the psalm. a sǽculo → *desde sempre* (row, open; 24:6, 118:52 applied). The pair echoes *sempre … sempre* as the Latin echoes *sǽculo … sǽculum*. MS1932 *por todos os séculos dos séculos* is in sǽculum sǽculi's wording (D27) and drops *a*.

options.label: desde sempre e para todo o sempre

forms.asaeculo: desde sempre e para todo o sempre

options.label: de eternidade em eternidade
options.note: DRB 'from eternity to eternity'; *eternidade* is not the Latin's word, and it drops D37's form.

decisions.why: The close of Book I (MS1932's note: a doxology distinct from the psalm), repeated at 71:19, 88:53, 105:48 (grep). *Fiat* alone, with no subject, is the Latin's (and the Greek's γένοιτο) rendering of the Hebrew *amen*. The glossary's *Seja* is for a jussive with a subject; *Seja, seja* is not Portuguese; *Faça-se* failed the stylist twice in Ps 118. *Assim seja* is the Portuguese of the Latin *fiat* in prayer (MS1932, DRB 'So be it'); *assim* is supplied, as grammar. *Amém* is the Hebrew, not the Latin.

choices.40:2: egénus → *necessitado*, pauper → *pobre* (glossary, D38; as 34:10b *o necessitado e o pobre*). *in die mala* → *no dia mau* (DRB 'the evil day', MS1932). *liberábit eum Dóminus* → *o livrará o Senhor*, the build of 33:20.
choices.40:3: beátum fáciat → *o faça bem-aventurado* (D19; the beátus row names 40:3). consérvet → *conserve* (15:1, 36:28). tradere → *entregar* (9:35a, 26:12, 118:121). The versicle for the Pope (Preces.txt) — it reads alone.
choices.40:4: lectus → *leito*, dolor → *dor*, infirmitas → *enfermidade* (15:4a). *super lectum* → *sobre o leito* (MS1932).
choices.40:5: Ego dixi → *Eu disse* (38:2). *Miserére mei* → *tende piedade de mim* (formula). sanáre → *curar* (6:3, 29:3). *peccávi tibi* → *pequei contra vós* (DRB, MS1932). *Sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi* is a short responsory (Major/Minor Special, Preces — grep): *Curai a minha alma, porque pequei contra vós* reads alone.
choices.40:6: períre → *perecer* (row). The quoted question keeps its capital, as the Latin.
choices.40:7: vana loqui → *falar coisas vãs* (11:3). congregáre → *juntar* (32:7, 34:15, 38:7b); the perfect kept (MS1932's imperfect *acumulava* not taken). ingrédi here is entering a room, not walking (14:2, 37:7 *andar*): the verse sets *ingrediebátur* against 40:7b *egrediebátur foras*.
choices.40:8: The anaphora *Contra mim … contra mim* kept at the head of both colons, as the Latin.
choices.40:9: constitúere → *estabelecer* (2:6, 4:10, 8:6, 9:21, 17:44, 117:27b). iníquus → *iníquo*. Natural order: the verb first.
choices.40:10: homo pacis meæ → *o homem da minha paz*: the Hebraism kept (MS1932 explains: *da minha intimidade*); 36:37 *hómini pacífico* → *homem de paz*. speráre in → *esperar em* (D36). édere → *comer* (row).
choices.40:11: Tu autem, Dómine → *Vós, porém, Senhor* (3:4). retribúere → *retribuir* (17:21, 30:24); *eu* supplied so the first person is heard after two imperatives. Holy Saturday's responsory (Quad6-6) quotes the second colon with *Et resúscita me*.
choices.40:12: cognóvi quóniam → *conheci que* (118:75). *gaudébit … super me* is ἐπιχαρῇ ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ, the Greek of *supergaudére* (34:19, 34:24, 37:17 — read in consult/parallels/ps034.md, ps037.md), so the same Portuguese: *não se alegrará à minha custa* (also 29:2). The second *quóniam* → *porque* (DRB 'because').
choices.40:13: Me autem → *Mas a mim* (the fronted object; *mas eu* is ego autem's). suscípere → *amparar* (D19; 29:2 *suscepísti me → me amparastes*).
choices.40:14: Benedíctus Dóminus → *Bendito o Senhor* (27:6, 30:22). *Deus Israël* → *Deus de Israel*, in apposition. The same verse closes Book IV (105:48, with *et dicet omnis pópulus*) and the Benedictus opens with *Benedíctus Dóminus Deus Israël*: whoever translates them should copy this wording.
choices.40:7b: The ruling on *in idípsum* is local (D9 deferred); see decision `idipsum`. The second colon is +1 on the Latin.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm40.txt, 14 prayed verses (40:2–40:14 with 40:7b; DO writes the second 40:7 without the letter; no 40:1, the titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): 40:2 an Alleluia verse and Gradual (missa Tempora/Pent01-0a, Sancti/04-28, 07-18; office of St John Baptist de Rossi); 40:3 the versicle for the Pope (Preces.txt); 40:5 the short responsory *Sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi* (Major and Minor Special, Preces, Epi2-2, Pent02-5); 40:10 Maundy Thursday (Quad6-4 versicle and responsory, whose *ampliávit advérsum me* is another wording) and a Matins antiphon (Pent02-5); 40:11b Holy Saturday (Quad6-6); 40:13 an Offertory (missa Sancti/06-21) and Hildegard's office. Jn 13:18 fetched from the Clementine (consult/bolls-VULG-43-13.json). Not in the Diurnal Monástico parallels. The Hetzenauer print read is skipped and owed.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps040.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Formulas checked with ps038/xref.py and ps005/grep_latin.py. Rulings applied: D3 has no place (no *exaudíre*), D5 none (no *confitéri*); D19 (beátus, suscípere), D23 (in ætérnum), D36 (speráre in), D37 (usque in sǽculum), D38 (egénus kept *necessitado* beside *pobre*; no *inops* here), D39 (super me → contra mim). Latin readings kept against the Greek: 40:3 *in ánimam* (not 'hands'); 40:7b *in idípsum* joined to his speaking, not to the whispering. Tests for the readers: *entende o necessitado*, *o vivifique*, *à alma dos seus inimigos*, *lhe leve socorro*, *Revolvestes toda a sua cama*, *Ele saía para fora*, *no mesmo sentido*, *pensavam em males para mim*, *tornará a ressurgir*, *o homem da minha paz*, *a sua rasteira*, *ressuscitai-me*, *me quisestes*, *por causa da inocência*, *assim seja, assim seja*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 40:2 first colon +4 (*Bem-aventurado* and *necessitado*, the settled words), 40:14 second +4 (*assim seja* twice for *fiat* twice), 40:9 first +3, 40:12 second +3 (*à minha custa*, the formula), 40:7 first −4, 40:12 first −3; accepted. Rhyme 40:7b / 40:8 (*fim … mim*) mended before any reader: *no mesmo sentido*. Cadences: several oxytone finals where the Latin is paroxytone (*Senhor*, *mim*, *vós*); allowed by rule 4.
